literature.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 两种 mAb(1G2 和 4E5)可识别 RABV G 蛋白中的最小线性表位 (AEDFVEVHLP)。生物信息学分析揭示了该表位在不同 RABV 基因型中的高度保守替换。该表位定位于 G 蛋白表面上暴露于溶剂的 α 螺旋构象。 [10.1007/s00430-026-00887-x]
在猫中,疫苗 诱导针对三种病原体的中和抗体,并且免疫猫在 FHV-1 和 FCV 攻击后表现出较温和的临床症状和较轻的组织病理学病变。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728426]
该测定显示出广泛的稳健性、精确度、线性下/上限和稳定性。检出限为2.63 IU/mL,变异系数小于20%。结果与ELISA和RFFIT高度一致,kappa值分别为0.74和0.82。 [10.1128/jcm.00877-26]
Western blot 分析显示,SAD-B19 衍生的 G 蛋白表现出比 CVS11 衍生的 G 蛋白更高的表观分子量。 [10.3390/vetsci13090919]
该模型证明了解的正性和有界性,并计算了犬类种群的基本繁殖数($$R_{0d}$$)。通过 Adams Bashforth Moulton 预测校正器方法进行数值模拟以验证理论结果。 [10.1038/s41598-026-67028-5]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Two mAbs (1G2 and 4E5) recognized a minimal linear epitope (AEDFVEVHLP) in the G protein of RABV. Bioinformatic analysis revealed highly conserved substitutions of this epitope across diverse RABV genotypes. The epitope was localized to a solvent-exposed α-helical conformation on the G protein surface. [10.1007/s00430-026-00887-x]

In cats, the vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies against the three pathogens, and immunized cats showed milder clinical signs and less severe histopathological lesions following FHV-1 and FCV challenge. [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728426]

The assay showed broad robustness, precision, lower/upper limit of linearity, and stability. The limit of detection was 2.63 IU/mL, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%. The results were highly consistent with ELISA and RFFIT, with kappa values of 0.74 and 0.82, respectively. [10.1128/jcm.00877-26]
Western blot analysis revealed that the SAD-B19-derived G protein exhibited a higher apparent molecular weight than the CVS11-derived G protein. [10.3390/vetsci13090919]

The model proved the positivity and boundedness of solutions and calculated the basic reproduction number of the canine population ($$R_{0d}$$). Numerical simulations through the Adams Bashforth Moulton predictor corrector method were conducted to validate the theoretical results. [10.1038/s41598-026-67028-5]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
两种 mAb(1G2 和 4E5)可识别 RABV G 蛋白中的最小线性表位 (AEDFVEVHLP)。生物信息学分析揭示了该表位在不同 RABV 基因型中的高度保守替换。该表位定位于 G 蛋白表面上暴露于溶剂的 α 螺旋构象。
在猫中,疫苗 诱导针对三种病原体的中和抗体,并且免疫猫在 FHV-1 和 FCV 攻击后表现出较温和的临床症状和较轻的组织病理学病变。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728426]。
该测定显示出广泛的稳健性、精确度、线性下/上限和稳定性。检出限为2.63 IU/mL,变异系数小于20%。结果与ELISA和RFFIT高度一致,kappa值分别为0.74和0.82。 [10.1128/jcm.00877-26]。
Western blot 分析显示,SAD-B19 衍生的 G 蛋白表现出比 CVS11 衍生的 G 蛋白更高的表观分子量。 [10.3390/vetsci13090919]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

Two mAbs (1G2 and 4E5) recognized a minimal linear epitope (AEDFVEVHLP) in the G protein of RABV. Bioinformatic analysis revealed highly conserved substitutions of this epitope across diverse RABV genotypes.

In cats, the vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies against the three pathogens, and immunized cats showed milder clinical signs and less severe histopathological lesions following FHV-1 and FCV challenge.
The assay showed broad robustness, precision, lower/upper limit of linearity, and stability. The limit of detection was 2.63 IU/mL, and the coefficient of variation was less than 20%.
Western blot analysis revealed that the SAD-B19-derived G protein exhibited a higher apparent molecular weight than the CVS11-derived G protein. [10.3390/vetsci13090919].

papers.title: Identification of a novel conserved B-cell epitope in the glycoprotein of rabies virus.
papers.abstract: Rabies virus (RABV), a single-stranded RNA virus, invades the central nervous system and causes acute, zoonotic diseases worldwide. The glycoprotein (G) of RABV is the only surface antigen responsible for inducing potent neutralizing antibodies, making it a key target for medical countermeasures. In this study, two anti-G protein monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) were prepared using hybridoma cell technology, with their high specificity and robust reactivity validated by indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (i-ELISA), indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and Western blot. Through systematic epitope mapping using a series of truncated G protein fragments, two mAbs (1G2 and 4E5) were found to recognize a minimal linear epitope, AEDFVEVHLP (amino acids 412-421) through Dot-ELISA and i-ELISA. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis further defined the core binding residues within this epitope as 412 Ala-Glu-Asp-Phe-Val 416 , 418 Val, 420 Leu, and 421 Pro. Bioinformatic analysis with MEGA software revealed highly conserved with conservative substitutions of this epitope across diverse RABV of genotype 1. Homology modeling with SWISS-MODEL localized the epitope " 412 AEDFVEVHLP 421 " to a solvent-exposed α-helical conformation on the G protein surface. And this epitope is located in the extracellular C-terminal region, Prior studies have demonstrated that this region plays a role in stabilizing the trimerization of the rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG). In conclusion, our study identifies a novel, highly conserved with conservative substitutions linear B-cell epitope on the RABV glycoprotein, providing a precise molecular target for the rational design of next-generation epitope-based vaccines and specific diagnostic tools.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify a novel conserved B-cell epitope in the glycoprotein of rabies virus (RABV) to inform the design of next-generation vaccines and diagnostic tools. papers.title_zh: 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白中新型保守 B 细胞表位的鉴定。
papers.source_body_en: Rabies virus (RABV), a single-stranded RNA virus, invades the central nervous system and causes acute, zoonotic diseases worldwide. The glycoprotein (G) of RABV is the only surface antigen responsible for inducing potent neutralizing antibodies, making it a key target for medical countermeasures. In this study, two anti-G protein monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) were prepared using hybridoma cell technology, with their high specificity and robust reactivity validated by indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (i-ELISA), indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) and Western blot. Through systematic epitope mapping using a series of truncated G protein fragments, two mAbs (1G2 and 4E5) were found to recognize a minimal linear epitope, AEDFVEVHLP (amino acids 412-421) through Dot-ELISA and i-ELISA. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis further defined the core binding residues within this epitope as 412 Ala-Glu-Asp-Phe-Val 416 , 418 Val, 420 Leu, and 421 Pro. Bioinformatic analysis with MEGA software revealed highly conserved with conservative substitutions of this epitope across diverse RABV of genotype 1. Homology modeling with SWISS-MODEL localized the epitope " 412 AEDFVEVHLP 421 " to a solvent-exposed α-helical conformation on the G protein surface. And this epitope is located in the extracellular C-terminal region, Prior studies have demonstrated that this region plays a role in stabilizing the trimerization of the rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG). In conclusion, our study identifies a novel, highly conserved with conservative substitutions linear B-cell epitope on the RABV glycoprotein, providing a precise molecular target for the rational design of next-generation epitope-based vaccines and specific diagnostic tools.

papers.title: Immunogenicity evaluation of recombinant rabies virus-vectored multivalent vaccines expressing feline calicivirus VP1 and feline herpesvirus 1 gB/gD genes.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Feline calicivirus (FCV) and feline herpesvirus 1 (FHV-1) are major pathogens threatening feline health, and prophylactic immunity remains the primary preventive approach. To develop a safe and effective multivalent vaccine against the two viruses, two recombinant rabies virus (RABV) vaccines expressing the FCV VP1 and FHV-1 gB/gD genes were constructed. The exogenous genes showed stable inheritance following serial viral passages, and the recombinant RABVs exhibited growth kinetics comparable to the parental strain, with a delayed peak titer. After verifying the viral pathogenicity, the recombinant RABV vaccines elicited specific IgG antibodies against VP1, gB, and gD, as well as neutralizing antibodies against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in mice. Immunized mice were also protected against lethal RABV challenge. In cats, the vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies against the three pathogens, and immunized cats showed milder clinical signs and less severe histopathological lesions following FHV-1 and FCV challenge. Collectively, these findings indicate that the two recombinant vaccines induce robust humoral immune responses against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in both mice and cats and confer protection against viral challenges.

source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Feline calicivirus (FCV) and feline herpesvirus 1 (FHV-1) are major pathogens threatening feline health, and prophylactic immunity remains the primary preventive approach. To develop a safe and effective multivalent vaccine against the two viruses, two recombinant rabies virus (RABV) vaccines expressing the FCV VP1 and FHV-1 gB/gD genes were constructed. The exogenous genes showed stable inheritance following serial viral passages, and the recombinant RABVs exhibited growth kinetics comparable to the parental strain, with a delayed peak titer. After verifying the viral pathogenicity, the recombinant RABV vaccines elicited specific IgG antibodies against VP1, gB, and gD, as well as neutralizing antibodies against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in mice. Immunized mice were also protected against lethal RABV challenge. In cats, the vaccines induced neutralizing antibodies against the three pathogens, and immunized cats showed milder clinical signs and less severe histopathological lesions following FHV-1 and FCV challenge. Collectively, these findings indicate that the two recombinant vaccines induce robust humoral immune responses against FCV, FHV-1, and RABV in both mice and cats and confer protection against viral challenges.

papers.title: Mathematical analysis and passive control strategies for a fractional-order dog-to-human rabies model in danger zones
papers.abstract: Abstract Rabies is an invariably fatal zoonosis and a serious public health problem among dogs and humans within the danger zones due to large concentrations of stray dog populations. In order to provide insights into the transmission dynamics of the disease between dogs and humans, we present in this paper a new fractional-order SEIVQRD compartmental model using Caputo derivative. While in most traditional SEIR models it is difficult to investigate the role of control interventions, we explicitly incorporate the roles of various passive control methods such as mass vaccination of dogs and human post and pre exposure prophylaxis. The use of fractional calculus allows one to account for the nonlocal properties and hereditary effects in the highly variable incubation period of the virus. We prove some important properties of the model such as positivity and boundedness of solutions and calculation of the basic reproduction number of the canine population ( $$R_{0d}$$ ). It is proved that the disease free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable when $$R_{0d} . Moreover, through normalization of sensitivity analysis, it is found that canine vaccination is the most dominant parameter for controlling the epidemic threshold and hence preventing human death. Lastly, numerical simulation through Adams Bashforth Moulton predictor corrector method has been done to prove the theoretical results.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 狂犬病 是一种致命的 人兽共患病,并且由于流浪狗种群大量集中,对危险区域内的狗和人类来说是一个严重的公共卫生问题。为了深入了解狗和人类之间疾病的 传播 动力学,我们在本文中提出了一种使用 Caputo 导数的新分数阶 SEIVQRD 区室模型。虽然在大多数传统 SEIR 模型中很难研究控制干预的作用,但我们明确纳入了各种被动控制方法的作用,例如狗的质量 疫苗接种 和人类暴露后和暴露前预防。分数阶微积分的使用可以解释病毒高度可变的潜伏期中的非局部特性和遗传效应。我们证明了模型的一些重要属性,例如解的正性和有界性以及犬类种群基本繁殖数的计算($$R_{0d}$$)。证明当 $$R_{0d} 时,无病均衡全局渐近稳定。此外,通过敏感性分析的归一化,发现犬疫苗接种是控制流行阈值从而防止人类死亡的最主要参数。最后通过Adams Bashforth Moulton预测修正法进行数值模拟,验证了理论结果。

papers.title: A pseudovirus-based neutralizing antibody assay for measuring neutralizing antibody against rabies virus
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To establish a laboratory detection assay for a human neutralizing antibody (NAb) against rabies virus and to evaluate its efficiency in human serum samples. A pseudovirus pXN2‐RABV‐G harboring the RABV G gene was applied. The precision, robustness, linearity, stability, inclusivity, and limit of detection of the assay were evaluated. papers.title: Rabies Virus Glycoprotein G Variation Is Associated with Neurovirulence and Reduced Vamp2 Abundance in a Mouse Model of Direct CNS Infection
papers.abstract: Rabies virus causes fatal neurological disease, but the mechanisms by which its glycoprotein G influences neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. In this study, we rescued two recombinant RABV LBNSE strains carrying G proteins from either the attenuated SAD-B19 strain or the virulent CVS11 strain, designated as rLBNSE-SfG and rLBNSE-CfG, respectively. Infection of primary mouse neurons and challenge experiments in mice showed that rLBNSE-CfG was associated with increased early neuronal infectivity and greater neurovirulence after intracerebral (i.c.) injection. Western blot analysis revealed that the SAD-B19-derived G protein exhibited a higher apparent molecular weight than the CVS11-derived G protein. Bioinformatic analysis identified strain-specific differences in putative post-translational modification sites, which may contribute to the observed migration difference. Quantitative proteomic analysis of mouse brain tissue showed that proteins downregulated in the rLBNSE-CfG group were enriched in synaptic vesicle cycle-related pathways and synapse-associated Gene Ontology (GO) terms. Integrated analysis identified a SNARE-associated module containing Snap25, Stx1a, and Vamp2, among which Vamp2 was significantly reduced in the rLBNSE-CfG group. In primary neurons, reduced Vamp2 abundance was associated with the extracellular domain of CVS11 G protein. These findings associate CVS11-derived G protein variation with reduced Vamp2 abundance and a presynaptic vesicle-related proteomic signature, although whether these molecular alterations directly impair synaptic vesicle release remains to be determined.

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白 G 变异与直接中枢神经系统感染小鼠模型中的神经毒力和 Vamp2 丰度降低相关
papers.source_body_en: Rabies virus causes fatal neurological disease, but the mechanisms by which its glycoprotein G influences neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. In this study, we rescued two recombinant RABV LBNSE strains carrying G proteins from either the attenuated SAD-B19 strain or the virulent CVS11 strain, designated as rLBNSE-SfG and rLBNSE-CfG, respectively. Infection of primary mouse neurons and challenge experiments in mice showed that rLBNSE-CfG was associated with increased early neuronal infectivity and greater neurovirulence after intracerebral (i.c.) injection. Western blot analysis revealed that the SAD-B19-derived G protein exhibited a higher apparent molecular weight than the CVS11-derived G protein. Bioinformatic analysis identified strain-specific differences in putative post-translational modification sites, which may contribute to the observed migration difference. Quantitative proteomic analysis of mouse brain tissue showed that proteins downregulated in the rLBNSE-CfG group were enriched in synaptic vesicle cycle-related pathways and synapse-associated Gene Ontology (GO) terms. Integrated analysis identified a SNARE-associated module containing Snap25, Stx1a, and Vamp2, among which Vamp2 was significantly reduced in the rLBNSE-CfG group. In primary neurons, reduced Vamp2 abundance was associated with the extracellular domain of CVS11 G protein. These findings associate CVS11-derived G protein variation with reduced Vamp2 abundance and a presynaptic vesicle-related proteomic signature, although whether these molecular alterations directly impair synaptic vesicle release remains to be determined.
papers.abstract_zh: 狂犬病病毒 会导致致命的神经系统疾病,但其糖蛋白 G 影响神经元功能障碍的机制仍不完全清楚。在这项研究中,我们从减毒的SAD-B19毒株或强毒的CVS11毒株中拯救了两种携带G蛋白的重组RABV LBNSE毒株,分别命名为rLBNSE-SfG和rLBNSE-CfG。原代小鼠神经元的感染和小鼠攻击实验表明,rLBNSE-CfG 与脑内 (i.c) 注射后早期神经元感染性增加和神经毒力增强相关。Western blot 分析显示,SAD-B19 衍生的 G 蛋白表现出比 CVS11 衍生的 G 蛋白更高的表观分子量。生物信息分析确定了假定的翻译后修饰位点的菌株特异性差异,这可能导致观察到的迁移差异。小鼠脑组织的定量蛋白质组学分析表明,rLBNSE-CfG 组中下调的蛋白质在突触小泡周期相关通路和突触相关基因本体 (GO) 术语中富集。综合分析发现,SNARE相关模块包含Snap25、Stx1a和Vamp2,其中Vamp2在rLBNSE-CfG组中显着减少。在原代神经元中,Vamp2 丰度的减少与 CVS11 G 蛋白的胞外结构域相关。这些发现将 CVS11 衍生的 G 蛋白变异与 Vamp2 丰度减少和突触前囊泡相关蛋白质组特征联系起来,尽管这些分子改变是否直接损害突触囊泡释放仍有待确定。

papers.title: Immunogenicity of Single-visit, Two-site Intradermal Pre-exposure Rabies Prophylaxis in Children: A Prospective Interventional Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic countries, particularly among children. Simplified pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) schedules may improve feasibility and access in resource-limited settings and facilitate the integration of rabies vaccination into routine childhood immunization, school-based and community-based vaccination programs in rabies-endemic regions. However, pediatric data on single-visit, 2-site intradermal PrEP regimens remain limited. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP regimen in children 1-18 years of age on days 28 and 180. METHODS: This prospective single-arm study enrolled healthy children 1-18 years old at a tertiary care center. Participants received a single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP regimen with a Vero cell culture rabies vaccine (RABIVAX-S®). Anti-rabies glycoprotein immuglobulin G antibody concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and rabies virus neutralizing antibody concentrations were estimated by Rapid Fluorescent Focus Inhibition Test at baseline, day 28 and day 180. Participants with rabies virus neutralizing antibody concentrations <0.5 IU/mL at day 28 or day 180 received 2 intradermal booster doses on days 0 and 3 after laboratory results became available and participants returned for follow-up, followed by repeat antibody assessment 7 days after the first booster dose. The primary outcome was seroprotection (≥0.5 IU/mL). RESULTS: Forty-eight children were enrolled, of whom 44 were evaluated on day 28. The enrolled cohort comprised participants 2-15 years old. On day 28, 40/44 (90.9%) achieved protective antibody concentrations (≥0.5 IU/mL). Among 40 participants included in the day 180 analysis, 27 (67.5%) maintained protective concentrations. All participants with insufficient concentrations (n = 4 on day 28, n = 13 on day 180) demonstrated robust anamnestic responses following booster administration, achieving 100% seroprotection within 7 days. The regimen was well tolerated, with only mild local adverse events reported. CONCLUSIONS: Single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP demonstrated high early seroprotection and preserved immunologic priming despite declining antibody concentrations at 6 months. These findings support further evaluation of simplified pediatric PrEP regimens in larger controlled studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 仍然是流行国家的主要公共卫生问题,特别是儿童。然而,关于单次就诊、2 个部位皮内暴露前预防 (PrEP) 方案的儿科数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性单组研究招募了三级护理中心 1-18 岁的健康儿童。登记的队列研究由2-15岁的参与者组成。参与者接受了单次、2 个部位皮内 狂犬病 PrEP 方案以及 Vero 细胞培养物 狂犬病 疫苗 (RABIVAX-S®)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用酶联免疫吸附测定法测量抗 狂犬病 糖蛋白免疫球蛋白 G 抗体浓度,并通过快速荧光聚焦抑制测试在基线、第 28 天和第 180 天估计 狂犬病病毒 中和抗体浓度。在第 28 天或第 180 天 狂犬病病毒 中和抗体浓度 <0.5 IU/mL 的参与者在第 0 天接受 2 次皮内加强剂量3 次是在实验室结果出来且参与者返回进行随访后,在第一次加强剂量后 7 天进行重复抗体评估。主要结局是血清保护(≥0.5 IU/mL)。
elements_zh.main_results: 入组了 48 名儿童,其中 44 名在第 28 天进行了评估。第 28 天,40/44 (90.9%) 达到了保护性抗体浓度 (≥0.5 IU/mL)。在 180 天分析中纳入的 40 名参与者中,27 名 (67.5%) 保持了保护浓度。所有浓度不足的参与者(第 28 天 n = 4,第 180 天 n = 13)在加强注射后表现出强烈的记忆反应,在 7 天内实现 100% 血清保护。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 6 个月时抗体浓度下降,但单次 2 部位皮内 狂犬病 PrEP 表现出较高的早期血清保护作用和保留的免疫启动作用。这些发现支持在更大的对照研究中进一步评估简化的儿科 PrEP 方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持在资源有限的环境中可能使用简化的 狂犬病 暴露前预防计划,促进将 狂犬病 狂犬病 纳入常规儿童免疫计划。该方案对儿童的安全性和有效性可能会为未来预防 狂犬病 的公共卫生策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单臂设计,没有比较组,这限制了评估该方案相对于其他 疫苗接种 方法的疗效的能力。由于缺乏对照组和潜在的偏见,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 儿童单次、两部位皮内预暴露 狂犬病 预防的免疫原性:一项前瞻性干预研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic countries, particularly among children. Simplified pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) schedules may improve feasibility and access in resource-limited settings and facilitate the integration of rabies vaccination into routine childhood immunization, school-based and community-based vaccination programs in rabies-endemic regions. However, pediatric data on single-visit, 2-site intradermal PrEP regimens remain limited. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of a single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP regimen in children 1-18 years of age on days 28 and 180. METHODS: This prospective single-arm study enrolled healthy children 1-18 years old at a tertiary care center. Participants received a single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP regimen with a Vero cell culture rabies vaccine (RABIVAX-S®). Anti-rabies glycoprotein immuglobulin G antibody concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and rabies virus neutralizing antibody concentrations were estimated by Rapid Fluorescent Focus Inhibition Test at baseline, day 28 and day 180. Participants with rabies virus neutralizing antibody concentrations <0.5 IU/mL at day 28 or day 180 received 2 intradermal booster doses on days 0 and 3 after laboratory results became available and participants returned for follow-up, followed by repeat antibody assessment 7 days after the first booster dose. The primary outcome was seroprotection (≥0.5 IU/mL). RESULTS: Forty-eight children were enrolled, of whom 44 were evaluated on day 28. The enrolled cohort comprised participants 2-15 years old. On day 28, 40/44 (90.9%) achieved protective antibody concentrations (≥0.5 IU/mL). Among 40 participants included in the day 180 analysis, 27 (67.5%) maintained protective concentrations. All participants with insufficient concentrations (n = 4 on day 28, n = 13 on day 180) demonstrated robust anamnestic responses following booster administration, achieving 100% seroprotection within 7 days. The regimen was well tolerated, with only mild local adverse events reported. CONCLUSIONS: Single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP demonstrated high early seroprotection and preserved immunologic priming despite declining antibody concentrations at 6 months. These findings support further evaluation of simplified pediatric PrEP regimens in larger controlled studies.

papers.title: Lyssavirus Nucleoprotein Induces GPAT4-Mediated CYB5R1 Depalmitoylation to Suppress Ferroptosis and Promote Viral Replication.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rabies virus (RABV) and other lyssaviruses exploit lipid droplet (LD) formation to evade host defenses, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that lyssavirus N proteins induce LD biogenesis by upregulating glycerol‐3‐phosphate acyltransferase 4 (GPAT4) expression and promoting its translocation to the LD surface, a conserved mechanism across the lyssavirus genus. Mechanistically, GPAT4‐mediated LD formation sequesters free fatty acids, leading to acyl‐protein thioesterase 1 (APT1)‐dependent depalmitoylation of NADH‐cytochrome B5 reductase 1 (CYB5R1) at Cys208 and Cys278. This post‐translational modification triggers autophagic degradation of CYB5R1, thereby impairing its ability to induce ferroptosis via two complementary pathways: nuclear receptor co‐activator 4 (NCOA4)‐mediated ferritinophagy and H 2 O 2 production. Conversely, diacylglycerol O‐acyltransferase (DGAT) inhibitors or GPAT4 knockdown restores CYB5R1 palmitoylation and stability, reinstates ferroptosis, and suppresses RABV infection. Our findings reveal a novel “ lyssavirus N‐GPAT4‐LD‐CYB5R1 palmitoylation” axis that modulates ferroptosis susceptibility, highlighting protein palmitoylation as a critical regulatory node in virus‐host interactions and identifying GPAT4 as a potential antiviral target.

papers.title: Immune Evasion by Neurotropic Viruses: Molecular Strategies, Cellular Targets, and Consequences for CNS Infection
papers.abstract: Neurotropic viruses have evolved sophisticated mechanisms to evade host immune responses within the central nervous system (CNS), enabling viral replication, persistence, latency, and neuropathogenesis while minimizing irreversible neuronal damage. Unlike peripheral tissues, the CNS requires tightly regulated antiviral immunity to balance effective pathogen control with the preservation of neural function. This review examines the diverse yet convergent immune evasion strategies employed by major neurotropic RNA and DNA viruses, including herpes simplex virus (HSV), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rabies virus (RABV), flaviviruses, alphaviruses, enteroviruses, and JC virus (JCV). We discuss viral interference with innate immune sensing pathways, including RIG-I-like receptors (RLRs) and cyclic GMP–AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS–STING) signaling, inhibition of type I interferon induction and Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK–STAT) signaling, modulation of interferon-stimulated effector mechanisms, and disruption of antigen presentation and adaptive immune surveillance. The review further highlights the distinct roles of viral latency, long-term persistence, neuronal–glial interactions, and metabolic reprogramming in facilitating prolonged infection within the CNS. Emerging evidence indicates that successful neurotropic viruses rarely achieve immune evasion through complete suppression of host defenses; instead, they fine-tune antiviral responses to preserve host cell viability while preventing viral clearance. Finally, we discuss current knowledge gaps and emphasize the need for advanced human-relevant models, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and systems-level approaches to better define virus–host interactions within the CNS. A deeper understanding of these integrated immune evasion networks may reveal novel therapeutic strategies that enhance antiviral immunity while limiting neuroinflammation and preserving neurological function.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, examining immune evasion strategies specific to this pathogen. The central question is how rabies virus evades host immune responses within the central nervous system (CNS) to facilitate infection and neuropathogenesis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of major neurotropic RNA and DNA viruses, including rabies virus. It discusses molecular strategies, cellular targets, and consequences for CNS infection, with an emphasis on immune evasion mechanisms. The evidence is derived from existing literature on these viruses, and the review method involves synthesizing findings from various studies to highlight common themes and mechanisms.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that rabies virus employs a range of immune evasion strategies, including interference with innate immune sensing pathways, inhibition of type I interferon induction, and modulation of interferon-stimulated effector mechanisms. These strategies allow the virus to persist and replicate within the CNS while minimizing host immune damage.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is emerging evidence suggesting that rabies virus does not achieve immune evasion through complete suppression of host defenses but rather fine-tunes antiviral responses to preserve host cell viability. The review also highlights the need for advanced human-relevant models and systems-level approaches to better understand virus–host interactions within the CNS.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of developing more sophisticated models to study rabies virus interactions with the host immune system. It also suggests that a deeper understanding of these mechanisms could lead to novel therapeutic strategies that enhance antiviral immunity while limiting neuroinflammation and preserving neurological function.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how rabies virus evades host immune responses within the central nervous system (CNS), enabling its replication and persistence. It highlights the virus's strategies, such as interference with innate immune sensing pathways and modulation of interferon responses, which allow it to avoid complete immune suppression. The review also identifies gaps in current knowledge and suggests the need for advanced models and systems-level approaches to better understand rabies virus–host interactions. These insights may inform future therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing antiviral immunity while minimizing neuroinflammation and preserving neurological function.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,研究针对该病原体的免疫逃避策略。核心问题是狂犬病病毒如何在中枢神经系统(CNS)内逃避宿主 免疫应答以促进感染和神经发病。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对主要的嗜神经 RNA 和 DNA 病毒(包括 狂犬病病毒)进行了全面分析。它讨论了中枢神经系统感染的分子策略、细胞靶点和后果,重点是免疫逃避机制。证据来自有关这些病毒的现有文献,审查方法涉及综合各种研究的结果,以突出共同的主题和机制。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,狂犬病病毒 采用了一系列免疫逃避策略,包括干扰先天免疫​​传感途径、抑制 I 型干扰素诱导以及调节干扰素刺激的效应机制。这些策略允许病毒在中枢神经系统内持续存在和复制,同时最大限度地减少 宿主 免疫损伤。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 新出现的证据表明,狂犬病病毒 并不是通过完全抑制 宿主 防御来实现免疫逃避,而是微调 抗病毒药物 反应以保留 宿主 细胞活力。该评论还强调需要先进的人类相关模型和系统级方法,以更好地了解中枢神经系统内病毒与 宿主 的相互作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调了开发更复杂的模型来研究 狂犬病病毒 与 宿主 免疫系统相互作用的重要性。它还表明,对这些机制的更深入了解可能会导致新的治疗策略,增强 抗病毒药物 免疫力,同时限制神经炎症和保留神经功能。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病,研究针对该病原体的免疫逃避策略。核心问题是狂犬病病毒如何在中枢神经系统(CNS)内逃避宿主 免疫应答以促进感染和神经发病。

papers.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis as a complementary vaccination strategy to reduce rabies in Kerala, India: a cost-effectiveness modelling study
papers.abstract: Background Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and dog vaccination continue to be the widely adopted vaccination strategy for rabies control in high-burden countries like India. To determine the public health and economic impacts of childhood pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) relative to existing strategies, we carried out a modelling analysis in the state of Kerala, India. Methods We adapted a probabilistic decision-tree model over a 10-year time horizon (2026–2035). This timeframe is sufficient for dog vaccination to interrupt rabies transmission and for protection to accrue from PrEP delivered through routine childhood immunisation. The model simulates interactions between dog vaccination, PrEP, and PEP to estimate health provider costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained, and net health benefit across a range of willingness-to-pay thresholds. Findings Assuming current practice of four-dose intradermal PEP and sub-optimal dog vaccination, we projected 431 rabies deaths (95% Prediction interval [PI] 353–523) and a cost of US$50.3 million over ten years, with dog vaccination responsible for almost 70% of deaths averted by this strategy. Routine childhood PrEP increased costs by US$10.5–36.5 million (INR 1.0–3.4 billion), depending on the regimen used, and cumulatively prevented only ten additional deaths beyond those averted by current practice. Incorporating PrEP was not optimal (probability ≤12%) across India's willingness-to-pay threshold. The intensified owned-dog vaccination strategy achieved the highest benefit at India's mean willingness-to-pay (739,420 QALYs; 28% probability of optimality), while adopting WHO's recommended abridged PEP regimen was the only cost-saving strategy (US$6.3 million saved; equivalent mortality to status quo). Comprehensive dog vaccination coverage of 70% combined with abridged PEP regimens became optimal at India's upper willingness-to-pay threshold, reducing deaths by 83% compared to current practice. Interpretation In high-PEP-access settings, PrEP is not cost-effective and provides negligible benefit. To maximise lives saved, PrEP should only be considered once gains from strengthening dog vaccination and PEP delivery have been exhausted. Funding Wellcome Trust; Indian Council of Medical Research - Department of Health Research (ICMR-DHR) International Fellowship for Senior Biomedical Scientists.

The intensified owned-dog vaccination strategy achieved the highest benefit at India's mean willingness-to-pay (739,420 QALYs; 28% probability of optimality), while adopting WHO's recommended abridged PEP regimen was the only cost-saving strategy (US$6.3 million saved; equivalent mortality to status quo). Comprehensive dog vaccination coverage of 70% combined with abridged PEP regimens became optimal at India's upper willingness-to-pay threshold, reducing deaths by 83% compared to current practice. Interpretation In high-PEP-access settings, PrEP is not cost-effective and provides negligible benefit. To maximise lives saved, PrEP should only be considered once gains from strengthening dog vaccination and PEP delivery have been exhausted. papers.title: Community Perceptions of Free-Roaming Dog Management, Public Health Risks, and Animal Welfare in Ongata Rongai, Kenya
papers.abstract: Free-roaming dogs create public health, environmental, and animal welfare challenges, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In Kenya, dogmediated rabies remains an important public health concern. Understanding community perceptions can inform locally appropriate dog population management within a One Health framework. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 106 eligible respondents in Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County, using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire. Descriptive statistics summarized respondent characteristics and perceptions. Associations between demographic characteristics and dichotomized perception outcomes were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test or Fisher's exact test where expected cell counts were small; Bonferroni adjustment was applied across 16 demographic comparisons. Results showed that respondents strongly supported community education on responsible dog ownership (95.3%), partnerships with animal welfare organizations and the local community (93.4%), increased county government investment (93.4%), and spaying and neutering (93.4%). Proper dog ownership was the most frequently selected single management option (42.5%). Most respondents perceived free-roaming dogs as sources of fear and insecurity (95.3%), environmental contamination (85.8%), disease or rabies transmission (82.1%), and dog-bite risk (76.4%). No demographic association remained statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Respondents favored humane, integrated approaches to free-roaming dog management and perceived stronger public health and welfare concerns. Responsible ownership, community education, vaccination, reproductive control, and multisectoral collaboration warrant consideration in locally appropriate programs for managing dog populations.
papers.journal: Journal of Animal Science and Applied Biology

papers.abstract_zh: 自由漫步的狗给公共卫生、环境和动物福利带来了挑战,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。在肯尼亚,狗介导的 狂犬病 仍然是一个重要的公共卫生问题。了解社区的看法可以为“同一个健康”框架内适合当地的犬只种群管理提供信息。使用结构化访谈问卷对 Kajiado 县 Ongata Rongai 的 106 名符合条件的受访者进行了横断面调查。描述性统计总结了受访者的特征和看法。使用皮尔逊卡方检验或费舍尔精确检验(其中预期细胞计数较小)评估人口特征和二分感知结果之间的关联;Bonferroni 调整适用于 16 个人口统计比较。结果显示,受访者强烈支持负责任养狗的社区教育(95.3%)、与动物福利组织和当地社区建立伙伴关系(93.4%)、增加县政府投资(93.4%)以及绝育和绝育(93.4%)。适当的养狗是最常选择的单一管理选项(42.5%)。大多数受访者认为自由漫游的狗是恐惧和不安全感(95.3%)、环境污染(85.8%)、疾病或狂犬病 传播(82.1%)和狗咬伤风险(76.4%)的来源。Bonferroni 调整后,人口统计相关性不再具有统计学显着性。受访者赞成对自由漫游的狗进行人道、综合的管理方法,并认为对公共健康和福利有更强烈的关注。负责任的所有权、社区教育、疫苗接种、生殖控制和多部门合作值得在适合当地的狗群管理计划中考虑。

papers.title: Safety and immunogenicity of novel group A streptococcal peptide vaccines targeting cryptic epitopes (J8-K4S2 and P*17-K4S2): a first-in-human, double-blinded, phase 1 randomised controlled trial
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapidity and aggressiveness of many group A streptococcal ( Streptococcus pyogenes ) clinical syndromes highlight the urgent need for a vaccine. Two related combination cryptic epitope peptide vaccines, J8-CRM+K4S2-CRM (‘J8-K4S2’) and p*17-CRM+K4S2-CRM (‘p*17-K4S2’), are novel vaccine candidates under investigation. In this single-centred, two-stage, unblinded sentinel safety dosing, then randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial, 30 volunteers were recruited (NCT04882514). Ten volunteers (Stage 1) were given test doses of J8-K4S2 and then p*17-K4S2 in a staggered, unblinded fashion at weeks 0, 3 and 6 to confirm immediate safety of the products. This was followed by twenty volunteers (Stage 2) who were randomized to receive either of the trial vaccines, J8-K4S2 or p*17-K4S2, or comparator (RabAvert) vaccine following the same vaccination schedule. The primary outcome was vaccine safety; the secondary outcome was immunogenicity. Both vaccine candidates were well tolerated and elicited robust immune responses. The most common adverse events noted were transient injection site pain, injection site erythema, fatigue and headache. These were similar for those receiving either the novel vaccines or the rabies vaccine comparator. There were no high-grade attributable adverse events and no severe adverse events overall. Immunogenicity assessment by ELISA demonstrated that both vaccine candidates consistently induced strong and sustained antibody responses against their respective target antigens, J8 and p*17, with lower responses to K4S2 commensurate with the lower dose of K4S2 present in the vaccines. Both vaccines induced antibody responses to the surface of different strains of live S. All 20 participants who received the candidate vaccines achieved at least a 4-fold rise in J8- or p*17-specific antibody titers from baseline, demonstrating 100% seroconversion, while 90% also seroconverted to K4S2. Notably, these elevated antibody responses persisted for at least six months post-vaccination, remaining significantly above pre-immunisation levels, highlighting the durability of the immune response induced by both vaccines. The safety and immunogenicity profiles for J8-K4S2 and p*17-K4S2 were favourable and support ongoing development of these promising vaccine candidates.

papers.title: Epidemiology, risk factors, and prevention of animal bites injuries in Slovakia: an 18-year epidemiological analysis
papers.abstract: Background Animal bite injuries, predominantly from dogs, rank among the top 15 causes of nonfatal injuries globally. Since 2006, negligible number of cases of rabies were declared in Slovakia, lacks comprehensive national data on bite demographics and outcomes. Methods This Epidemiological study analysed 14,978 patient records (2006–2023) obtained from Slovak public health databases. Statistical analyses, including chi-square tests and linear regression, were used to evaluate trends in bite incidence, vaccination coverage, and associated risk factors. Results Between 2006 and 2023, 14,978 individuals sought treatment for animal exposures, with 88% of exposures attributed to domestic animals, primarily dogs (78.9%). Children aged 5–9 years and adults aged 25–34 years represented the highest-risk groups. The authors observed a significant downward trend in bite incidence over time ( β = −0.507, p = 0.002), with hands being the most commonly affected sites (41%). No human rabies cases were reported after 1990, and nationwide animal vaccination programs led to the near elimination of rabies by 2006. However, the authors recorded a 50% increase in bite incidents in the post-lockdown period (2022–2023), predominantly affecting males. The analysis demonstrated a significant negative temporal trend, with animal bite incidence decreasing by approximately 0.51 cases per 100,000 population per year ( β = −0.507, 95% CI: −0.82 to −0.19, p = 0.002). Conclusion Slovakia’s rabies control program represents a major public health success; however, animal exposures—particularly dog bites—remain a persistent problem. A temporary decline in bite incidence was observed during COVID-19 lockdowns, followed by a marked post-pandemic increase. papers.title: RABIES TREATMENT CASCADE, SURVEILLANCE GAPS, POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS ADHERENCE AND HEALTH-SYSTEM BARRIERS IN THE NIGER DELTA REGION OF NIGERIA: A SCOPING REVIEW
papers.abstract: Rabies remains a fatal yet vaccine-preventable zoonosis, with Nigeria accounting for an estimated 1,600-10,000 human deaths annually. Despite effective vaccines, weak surveillance systems, inadequate laboratory confirmation, and poor health-seeking behaviour obscure the true disease burden, particularly in southern states such as Akwa Ibom. Rabies remains an almost entirely preventable but near-uniformly fatal zoonosis, and dog-mediated transmission continues to impose a disproportionate burden on low-resource settings, with Nigeria ranked among the countries with the highest absolute rabies mortality worldwide Within Nigeria, the Niger Delta region presents a distinct combination of riverine geographic fragmentation, documented veterinary and surveillance capacity gaps, and health-system constraints that may shape a treatment cascade different from that described elsewhere in the country, yet no prior review has systematically synthesized this evidence. This scoping review, incorporating systematic elements, sought to consolidate and critically appraise available evidence on the rabies treatment cascade, surveillance gaps, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) adherence, and health-system barriers within the Niger Delta region of Nigeria. The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The evidence was charted across the population-concept-context (PCC) domains of rabies-exposed individuals, treatment-cascade and surveillance outcomes, and the Niger Delta setting, drawing on peer-reviewed literature, WHO and NCDC programmatic sources, and comparator studies from analogous Nigerian states. The results as evidenced, indicates a treatment cascade that leaks at multiple points rather than at a single stage: unprovoked bites disproportionately affecting children, inconsistent formal care-seeking, and highly variable PEP completion, including a documented instance in which no sampled Cross River victims completed a full regimen. Surveillance in the region has historically been passive and fragmented, with systematic real-time tracking only introduced in Cross River State in 2022. Recurrent barriers included PEP cost, facility distance, and workforce and community knowledge gaps. The Niger Delta's rabies burden appears sustained less by any single point of failure than by the absence of coordinated human-animal-environmental surveillance and financing structures. Emerging One Health coordination mechanisms piloted elsewhere in Nigeria offer a transferable, though yet unproven, template for the region.

papers.title_zh: 尼日利亚尼日尔三角洲地区的 狂犬病 治疗 级联、监测 差距、暴露后预防 依从性和卫生系统障碍:范围界定审查
papers.source_body_en: Rabies remains a fatal yet vaccine-preventable zoonosis, with Nigeria accounting for an estimated 1,600-10,000 human deaths annually. Despite effective vaccines, weak surveillance systems, inadequate laboratory confirmation, and poor health-seeking behaviour obscure the true disease burden, particularly in southern states such as Akwa Ibom. Rabies remains an almost entirely preventable but near-uniformly fatal zoonosis, and dog-mediated transmission continues to impose a disproportionate burden on low-resource settings, with Nigeria ranked among the countries with the highest absolute rabies mortality worldwide Within Nigeria, the Niger Delta region presents a distinct combination of riverine geographic fragmentation, documented veterinary and surveillance capacity gaps, and health-system constraints that may shape a treatment cascade different from that described elsewhere in the country, yet no prior review has systematically synthesized this evidence. This scoping review, incorporating systematic elements, sought to consolidate and critically appraise available evidence on the rabies treatment cascade, surveillance gaps, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) adherence, and health-system barriers within the Niger Delta region of Nigeria. The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The evidence was charted across the population-concept-context (PCC) domains of rabies-exposed individuals, treatment-cascade and surveillance outcomes, and the Niger Delta setting, drawing on peer-reviewed literature, WHO and NCDC programmatic sources, and comparator studies from analogous Nigerian states. The results as evidenced, indicates a treatment cascade that leaks at multiple points rather than at a single stage: unprovoked bites disproportionately affecting children, inconsistent formal care-seeking, and highly variable PEP completion, including a documented instance in which no sampled Cross River victims completed a full regimen. Surveillance in the region has historically been passive and fragmented, with systematic real-time tracking only introduced in Cross River State in 2022. Recurrent barriers included PEP cost, facility distance, and workforce and community knowledge gaps. The Niger Delta's rabies burden appears sustained less by any single point of failure than by the absence of coordinated human-animal-environmental surveillance and financing structures. Emerging One Health coordination mechanisms piloted elsewhere in Nigeria offer a transferable, though yet unproven, template for the region.
papers.abstract_zh: 狂犬病 仍然是一种致命的 疫苗 可预防的 人兽共患病,尼日利亚每年估计有 1,600-10,000 人死亡。尽管 疫苗 有效,但 疫苗 系统薄弱、实验室确认不足以及不良的求医行为掩盖了真正的疾病负担,特别是在阿夸伊博姆等南部各州。狂犬病 仍然是一种几乎完全可预防但几乎一致致命的 人兽共患病,由狗介导的 传播 继续对资源匮乏的地区造成不成比例的负担,尼日利亚是全球 狂犬病 死亡率 绝对值最高的国家之一。在尼日利亚境内,尼日尔三角洲地区呈现出河流地理破碎化、有记录的兽医和监测 能力差距和卫生系统限制可能会形成与该国其他地方描述的不同的 治疗 级联,但之前没有任何审查系统地综合了这一证据。这项范围界定审查纳入了系统性要素,旨在巩固和严格评估有关尼日利亚尼日尔三角洲地区 狂犬病 治疗 级联、监测 差距、暴露后预防 (PEP) 依从性和卫生系统障碍的现有证据。该审查遵循 Arksey 和 O'Malley 框架,并根据 PRISMA 范围界定审查扩展 (PRISMA-ScR) 进行报告。证据绘制在 狂犬病 暴露个体的人口-概念-背景 (PCC) 领域、治疗 级联和 监测 结果以及尼日尔三角洲环境中,借鉴了同行评审文献、WHO 和 NCDC 规划来源以及来自类似尼日利亚各州的比较研究。结果表明,治疗 级联在多个点而不是在单个阶段泄漏:无端咬伤对儿童的影响尤为严重,正规寻求护理的不一致,以及 PEP 完成情况的高度可变,包括有记录的实例,其中没有采样的 Cross River 受害者完成完整的治疗方案。该地区的 监测 历来都是被动且分散的,系统性实时跟踪直到 2022 年才在克罗斯河州引入。经常出现的障碍包括 PEP 成本、设施距离以及劳动力和社区知识差距。尼日尔三角洲的 狂犬病 负担似乎不是由任何单点故障造成的,而是由缺乏协调的人类-动物-环境 狂犬病 和融资结构造成的。在尼日利亚其他地方试点的新兴 One Health 协调机制为该地区提供了一个可转移但尚未得到证实的模板。

papers.title: Subregion-specific input organization of prefrontal-projecting basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and weakened striatal-NBM inhibitory transmission in 5xFAD mice.
papers.abstract: Basal forebrain cholinergic neurons regulate cortical activity and cognition and are vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the upstream circuits controlling projection-defined basal forebrain cholinergic populations remain incompletely understood. Here, we used projection-specific rabies-mediated monosynaptic tracing to map whole-brain inputs to medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC)-projecting cholinergic neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM) and horizontal limb of the diagonal band of Broca (HDB). mPFC-projecting NBM and HDB cholinergic neurons received broad but distinct input patterns. NBM cholinergic neurons received prominent striatal input, including input from D1-expressing medium spiny neurons, whereas HDB cholinergic neurons showed proportionally weaker striatal input and broader non-striatal contributions. Optogenetic electrophysiology confirmed that striatal inputs formed monosynaptic GABAergic inhibitory synapses onto NBM cholinergic neurons. This inhibitory transmission was weakened in 5xFAD mice, indicating impairment of a striatal-NBM inhibitory circuit in an AD mouse model. Together, these findings reveal subregion-specific input organization of mPFC-projecting basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and identify an amyloid-associated vulnerability of the striatal-NBM circuit.

papers.title_zh: 5xFAD 小鼠中前额叶投射基底前脑胆碱能神经元的亚区域特异性输入组织和减弱的纹状体 NBM 抑制 传播。
papers.source_body_en: Basal forebrain cholinergic neurons regulate cortical activity and cognition and are vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the upstream circuits controlling projection-defined basal forebrain cholinergic populations remain incompletely understood. Here, we used projection-specific rabies-mediated monosynaptic tracing to map whole-brain inputs to medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC)-projecting cholinergic neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM) and horizontal limb of the diagonal band of Broca (HDB). mPFC-projecting NBM and HDB cholinergic neurons received broad but distinct input patterns. NBM cholinergic neurons received prominent striatal input, including input from D1-expressing medium spiny neurons, whereas HDB cholinergic neurons showed proportionally weaker striatal input and broader non-striatal contributions. Optogenetic electrophysiology confirmed that striatal inputs formed monosynaptic GABAergic inhibitory synapses onto NBM cholinergic neurons. This inhibitory transmission was weakened in 5xFAD mice, indicating impairment of a striatal-NBM inhibitory circuit in an AD mouse model. Together, these findings reveal subregion-specific input organization of mPFC-projecting basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and identify an amyloid-associated vulnerability of the striatal-NBM circuit.

papers.title: Rabies awareness and knowledge among adults in an urban Indian setting: evidence from Jaipur, India
papers.abstract: Background: Rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms appear yet preventable if post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is completed in time. National data show that almost half of those who begin a vaccine course in India do not complete it. Whether Jaipur residents possess the specific knowledge that governs treatment completion had not been assessed. Methods: A cross-sectional survey used a bilingual questionnaire of ten factual knowledge items, administered online and face to face across Jaipur (September 2025 to February 2026). After exclusions, 349 adults were analysed. Results: General awareness was high: 99.4% would attend a hospital after a bite and 89.1% knew rabies is preventable if treated in time. However, life-critical procedural knowledge was weak. Only 37.8% knew that rabies cannot be cured once symptoms appear, while 43.8% believed a hospital could still cure it, making the incorrect belief more prevalent than the correct one. Only 26.5% knew vaccine-induced protection is not immediate, 57.3% knew the full course requires four or five injections, and 42.1% knew that mammals other than dogs transmit the virus. Mean knowledge score was 6.07 of 10 (SD 1.87); 22.3% scored poorly. Scores were higher among those with a dog bite in the family or social circle (p=0.003). Conclusions: High awareness coexists with critical gaps in the knowledge that determines survival: that rabies is incurable after symptom onset, that protection is not immediate, and that the course must be completed. Closing these gaps requires targeted communication at the point of post-exposure care, not broader awareness activity.
papers.journal: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health

papers.title_zh: 印度城市环境中成年人的 狂犬病 意识和知识:来自印度斋浦尔的证据
papers.source_body_en: Background: Rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms appear yet preventable if post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is completed in time. National data show that almost half of those who begin a vaccine course in India do not complete it. Whether Jaipur residents possess the specific knowledge that governs treatment completion had not been assessed. Methods: A cross-sectional survey used a bilingual questionnaire of ten factual knowledge items, administered online and face to face across Jaipur (September 2025 to February 2026). After exclusions, 349 adults were analysed. Results: General awareness was high: 99.4% would attend a hospital after a bite and 89.1% knew rabies is preventable if treated in time. However, life-critical procedural knowledge was weak. Only 37.8% knew that rabies cannot be cured once symptoms appear, while 43.8% believed a hospital could still cure it, making the incorrect belief more prevalent than the correct one. Only 26.5% knew vaccine-induced protection is not immediate, 57.3% knew the full course requires four or five injections, and 42.1% knew that mammals other than dogs transmit the virus. Mean knowledge score was 6.07 of 10 (SD 1.87); 22.3% scored poorly. Scores were higher among those with a dog bite in the family or social circle (p=0.003). Conclusions: High awareness coexists with critical gaps in the knowledge that determines survival: that rabies is incurable after symptom onset, that protection is not immediate, and that the course must be completed. Closing these gaps requires targeted communication at the point of post-exposure care, not broader awareness activity.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:一旦出现症状,狂犬病 几乎总是致命的,但如果及时完成 暴露后预防 (PEP),则可以预防。国家数据显示,在印度开始 疫苗 课程的人中有近一半没有完成课程。尚未评估斋浦尔居民是否具备管理 治疗 完成的具体知识。方法:一项横断面调查使用了包含十个事实知识项目的双语调查问卷,在斋浦尔进行了在线和面对面的调查(2025 年 9 月至 2026 年 2 月)。排除后,对 349 名成年人进行了分析。结果:总体认知度较高:99.4% 的人被咬后会去医院,89.1% 的人知道如果及时治疗,狂犬病 是可以预防的。然而,攸关生命的程序知识却很薄弱。只有37.8%的人知道狂犬病一旦出现症状就无法治愈,而43.8%的人认为医院仍然可以治愈它,这使得错误的信念比正确的信念更普遍。只有 26.5% 的人知道 疫苗 引起的保护不是立竿见影的,57.3% 的人知道整个疗程需要四到五次注射,42.1% 的人知道狗以外的哺乳动物会传播病毒。平均知识得分为 6.07(满分 10 分)(SD 1.87);22.3%的人得分较差。在家庭或社交圈中被狗咬伤的人得分较高 (p=0.003)。结论:高认知度与决定生存的知识中的关键差距并存:狂犬病 在症状出现后无法治愈,保护不能立即进行,并且必须完成疗程。缩小这些差距需要在暴露后护理时进行有针对性的沟通,而不是更广泛的意识活动。

news.content: Local News Sports Opinion NKY Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals HEALTH CDC reports outbreak of human rabies exposure. How to protect yourself Chad Murphy USA TODAY NETWORK Updated Sept. 11, 2026, 1:07 p.m. ET The CDC has warned of an increase in human exposure to rabies during the summer of 2026. Rabies is a fatal but preventable viral disease that affects the central nervous system. The disease is primarily spread to humans through bites and scratches from infected animals like bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes. Human exposure to rabies is on the rise this summer, warns the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. According to a CDC health advisory issued Sept. 10, "multiple United States jurisdictions" have reported increases in human exposure to rabies or animals in which rabies is less commonly reported since July 2026. The advisory notes "high-profile rabies outbreaks and mass rabies exposure events." Those outbreaks include one in North Carolina, where baby goats at a mobile petting zoo were infected with rabies. Visitors may have been exposed to rabies at 10 locations between July 28 and Aug. 27. The CDC received 17% more rabies-related inquiries from July to August 2026 than during the same period in 2025, including reports of mass exposure events involving more than one person. According to weekly pharmacy data as of Sept. 2, 2026, utilization for the two rabies vaccines and the two rabies immunoglobulins licensed in the United States increased by an estimated 33% and 76%, respectively, compared with the same time period last year. Here's how to protect yourself from rabies. What is rabies? Rabies is a fatal but preventable viral disease, according to its CDC entry. It primarily affects the central nervous system, leading to severe brain disease and death if medical care is not received before symptoms start. How is rabies spread? It can be spread to people and pets through the bites and scratches of an infected animal. What are the symptoms of rabies? It can take weeks or months from the time of exposure for symptoms of rabies to show. And once clinical signs appear, the disease is almost always fatal. The first symptoms of rabies may include: Flu-like illness including weakness or discomfort, fever, or headache Discomfort, prickling or an itching sensation at the site of the bite Symptoms of advanced rabies include: Anxiety Confusion Agitation Hallucinations Being very thirsty but panicked by fluids Having lots of saliva Aggressive behavior like thrashing and biting What animals carry rabies? Do mosquitoes carry rabies? More than 90% of reported cases of rabies in animals occur in wildlife. Rabies is found in many wildlife species, including: Bats Raccoons Skunks Foxes Rabies in dogs Rabid dogs in the Unites States are uncommon because of effective vaccination and control programs, the CDC states. Worldwide, however, domestic dogs are responsible for the roughly 70,000 human deaths from rabies each year. Who is at risk for rabies? People most at risk for rabies include: Travelers, especially in areas where rabid dogs are still a problem Outdoor enthusiasts who may come into contact with rabid wildlife Veterinary professionals, animal control workers, wildlife researchers or rehabilitators, agricultural workers or others who work in contact with animals. People who are at increased risk for rabies exposures may want to consider pre-exposure vaccination for increased protection. How can you prevent rabies? The CDC says human cases of rabies in the United States are rare, thanks to prevention efforts of veterinarians who vaccinate more than 90 million dogs and cats each year, wildlife management officials and public health professionals. More than 5 million vaccine baits are distributed yearly to wildlife to control rabies in animals. You can help prevent rabies by: Making sure your pets are up to date on their rabies vaccines. Keeping wildlife wild — stay away from wildlife for both human and animal safety. Calling animal control to remove stray animals from your neighborhood. Washing bites or scratches immediately with soap and water after possible rabies exposure. Seeking medical care urgently if you may have been exposed to rabies. news.content: KSN-TV Human rabies exposure cases on the rise, CDC warns Addy Bink 2 days ago (NEXSTAR) — After a summer marred by foodborne illnesses, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has issued a new, potentially alarming alert. In a Thursday advisory, the agency warned health care providers of an increase in reported cases of human exposure to rabid or possibly rabid animals, and errors with the administration of responsive care. Across July and August, the CDC reported a 17% increase in rabies-related inquiries compared to the same time in 2025. The agency pointed to “several high-profile rabies outbreaks and mass rabies exposure events,” saying that they serve as reminders “of performing careful rabies risk assessments and following evidence-based recommendations for administering” rabies post-exposure prophylaxis care, or PEP. Use of rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins is up 33% and 76%, respectively, this year, according to the CDC. Health officials in Suffolk, Virginia, on Thursday warned residents that a raccoon recently tested positive for rabies within city limits. A dog in Mire, Louisiana, tested positive for rabies, prompting a warning from local veterinarians. In Elmira, New York, officials reported this week that multiple cats and skunks have recently tested positive for the virus. A rabies-infected bat was found in a Yosemite showerhouse earlier this year. A bat in Raleigh, North Carolina, tested positive after residents rescued it from a lake, but health officials said the humans had minimal to no contact with it. Nearly 300 people in the state were also exposed to rabies via a mobile petting zoo’s baby goats, the health department said last week. Rabies isn’t uncommon in the U.S. Roughly 1.4 million Americans seek medical attention after possible exposure to rabies, according to the CDC. However, fewer than 10 people die of rabies annually, a massive improvement from the “several hundred” who would die of rabies each year prior to 1960. “Death is inevitable” once a patient starts experiencing symptoms, the World Health Organization warns. To avoid this, health officials strongly encourage anyone who believes they’ve been exposed to rabies to immediately seek care, which can include PEP. That process frequently includes washing the wound, vaccination and antibody treatments, which can prevent the rabies virus from spreading to the central nervous system. It can be expensive, though, with costs running between $11,000 and $14,000, per the CDC. The agency encouraged health care providers to adhere to PEP and other rabies guidance in Thursday’s alert. Others are advised to keep their pets up to date on rabies vaccines and to stay away from wildlife, especially those that are injured, sick, or dead. Bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes are most frequently implicated in rabies exposures in the U.S. If you or your pet interacts with any wildlife, “particularly if you’ve been bitten or scratched,” it’s recommended that you wash the wound immediately with soap and water and speak with a health care provider about the incident. Symptoms of rabies can begin with flu-like illnesses, including fever, headache, weakness, and discomfort, according to the CDC. If you were bitten, you may experience “discomfort, prickling, or an itching sensation.” It can take weeks or months for those symptoms to appear. Then, roughly two weeks later, severe disease typically sets in, the CDC explains. This can lead to anxiety, confusion, agitation, hallucinations, excess saliva, behaviors like thrashing and biting, and being thirsty but scared of fluids. Rabies was one of more than two dozen diseases the CDC paused diagnostic testing for earlier this year, but as of early September testing had resumed. Nexstar’s Michael Bartiromo contributed to this report. Ad Your Privacy Choices

A rabies-infected bat was found in Yosemite earlier this year, and a bat in Raleigh, North Carolina, tested positive in late 2026. The CDC also paused diagnostic testing for rabies earlier this year but resumed it by early September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The CDC's advisory applies to healthcare providers nationwide, with specific mentions of Suffolk, Virginia; Mire, Louisiana; Elmira, New York; and Yosemite and Raleigh, North Carolina. Health officials in Suffolk, Virginia, and Mire, Louisiana, also issued local warnings about rabies-positive animals. In Elmira, New York, multiple cats and skunks tested positive for the virus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The CDC reported a 17% increase in rabies-related inquiries compared to the same time in 2025. Rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins usage is up 33% and 76%, respectively. The CDC emphasized the importance of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to prevent the virus from spreading to the central nervous system, as symptoms can begin with flu-like illnesses and progress to severe disease within weeks or months.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC encouraged healthcare providers to adhere to PEP and other rabies guidance. Health officials advised keeping pets up to date on rabies vaccines and avoiding contact with wildlife, especially those that are injured, sick, or dead. The CDC also warned that death is inevitable once symptoms appear, but PEP can prevent this.

The CDC warned that death is inevitable once symptoms appear, but PEP can prevent this. news.title_zh: CDC 警告称,人类 狂犬病 暴露病例正在上升 - KSN.com
news.source_body_en: The CDC has issued a new alert warning of an increase in reported cases of human exposure to rabid or possibly rabid animals, with specific mentions of outbreaks in Suffolk, Virginia; Mire, Louisiana; and Elmira, New York. Across July and August 2026, rabies-related inquiries rose by 17% compared to the same period in 2025. The agency also noted a 33% increase in rabies vaccine use and a 76% rise in immunoglobulin use. Health officials emphasized the importance of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to prevent the virus from spreading to the central nervous system, as symptoms can begin with flu-like illnesses and progress to severe disease within weeks or months. The CDC warned that death is inevitable once symptoms appear, but PEP can prevent this. The agency also advised keeping pets up to date on rabies vaccines and avoiding contact with wildlife, especially those that are injured, sick, or dead. The CDC paused diagnostic testing for rabies earlier this year but resumed it by early September 2026.

(Source: WCAX) By Dorothy Sedovic Published: Sep. 11, 2026 at 11:51 AM EDT Share Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google (Gray News) - Federal health officials are issuing a warning after they’ve seen a jump in cases of human exposure to rabies and an increase in errors during rabies preventive treatments. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention issued a “Health Alert Network Health Advisory” in response to a recent uptick in human exposure to rabies or rabid animals. Rabies is a viral disease that is practically always fatal but preventable when the proper treatment is given before the patient shows symptoms. There were 17% more cases of “rabies-related inquiries” during July and August than there were during the same period last year, according to the CDC. The agency also reported a rise in “mass exposure” cases where more than one person was exposed to rabies or a rabid animal. Recently, nearly 300 people may have been exposed to rabies after interacting with goats at a mobile petting zoo in North Carolina. Three baby goats tested positive for rabies, while another goat was not tested but presumed to have rabies, according to the North Carolina State Laboratory of Public Health. A suspected rabid animal is believed to have attacked people in Lebanon, New Hampshire. There have been three reported attacks, with witnesses reporting the animal appeared to be unusually aggressive. Witnesses described the animal as either a gray fox or a fisher, but officials cannot confirm what it is. In Maryland, a large part of Cunningham Falls State Park was shut down in early August after a 19-year-old fisherman was attacked by a beaver that later tested positive for rabies. The attack was the second of its kind to happen at the park this summer. According to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, a 13-year-old swimmer was attacked by a beaver on July 26. That beaver also tested positive for rabies. A dead bat found in a popular campground at Yosemite National Park tested positive for rabies, although the park said there was no reported human contact with the animal. The CDC has also seen a rise in the use of preventive rabies treatment known as post-exposure prophylaxis or PEP. According to the CDC, eight state health departments have reported an increase in the use of rabies PEP. The agency also reported that the use of two rabies vaccines rose by 33% in September 2026 compared to last year while the use of two human rabies immunoglobulins rose by 76%. Along with the rise in preventive rabies treatment, the CDC has seen a rise in errors when administering the treatment. The CDC said errors can occur when assessing if a patient needs PEP. For example, someone who has previously been vaccinated for rabies would not need a dose of human rabies immunoglobulins. According to the CDC, these errors can lead to unnecessary treatments, potential adverse effects and avoidable costs. A typical course of PEP treatment can range from $11,000 to $14,000 per person. “Following rabies PEP administration guidance helps ensure that lifesaving vaccines are available for persons who need it and extraneous costs are avoided,” the CDC said. Other errors reported during preventive treatment include: Administering rabies vaccine in the wrong area Administering HRIG and vaccine in the same syringe or anatomical site Forgetting to give HRIG to someone who needs it Misclassifying previous vaccination history or immune status Using an incorrect rabies vaccine schedule Unnecessarily restarting the rabies vaccine series after a schedule deviation In order to prevent exposure to rabies, the CDC advises the public to stay away from wildlife. The agency says never to approach an animal that appears to be sick or wounded and to report it to local animal control instead. The CDC also recommends keeping your pets up to date on their rabies vaccines as well as keeping them away from wildlife as much as possible. Should you or your pet come in contact with a wild or unknown animal, particularly if you or your pet have been scratched or bitten, the CDC recommends: Washing the wound immediately with soap and water for 15 minutes Telling your doctor or veterinarian what animal it was and whether it showed signs of behavior outside the norm Talking with a health professional about your rabies risk and if you will need treatment If the animal was not your own pet, asking for its owner to provide proof of its up-to-date rabies vaccination Capturing or confining the animal if it is safe to do so and contacting local animal control Copyright 2026 Gray Local Media, Inc. analysis.brief_en: The CDC has reported a significant increase in human rabies exposures and treatment errors in the United States. In North Carolina, nearly 300 people may have been exposed to rabies after interacting with goats at a mobile petting zoo, with three baby goats testing positive and another presumed rabid. In New Hampshire, a suspected rabid animal attacked people, leading to three reported incidents. Maryland also saw two beavers test positive for rabies, with one attack at Cunningham Falls State Park. A dead bat found at Yosemite National Park tested positive, though no human contact was reported. The CDC noted a 33% rise in two rabies vaccines and a 76% increase in human rabies immunoglobulins in September 2026. Errors in administering rabies treatment include misclassifying vaccination history, incorrect schedules, and unnecessary restarts. The CDC is issuing guidance to prevent unnecessary treatments, adverse effects, and avoidable costs, advising the public to avoid contact with wildlife and report suspected rabid animals to local authorities.

news.content: Open menu NTD Television U.S.ChinaWorldPoliticsHealthBusinessEntertainmentSports More ●LIVE search EN▼ NTD Television NewsHealth News CDC Issues Health Alert Over Increase in Reported Human Rabies Exposures Reports of human rabies exposures have increased across the United States this summer, prompting health officials to warn doctors about proper treatment and administration. By Kelly McBride Ni | Published: 9/10/2026, 11:21:24 PM EDT The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention headquarters in Atlanta, Ga., on Aug. 25, 2023. (Madalina Vasiliu/The Epoch Times) Reports of human rabies exposures have increased across the United States this summer, prompting health officials to warn doctors about proper treatment and administration. “During the summer of 2026, reports of animal exposures and rabies post-exposure vaccinations have increased across the country,” the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said in a statement Sept. 10. Rabies is a zoonotic viral disease that is almost always fatal once symptoms develop. However, the CDC said it can be prevented if post-exposure prophylaxis is administered before symptoms appear. “Proper administration of rabies vaccine and human rabies immune globulin is critical to ensuring patients receive effective protection while avoiding unnecessary treatment, costs, and strain on supplies,” the CDC added. Use of the nation's two licensed rabies vaccines rose an estimated 33 percent compared with the same period last year, while use of human rabies immune globulin jumped 76 percent, according to weekly pharmacy data through Sept. 2, the CDC reported. The CDC also released separate updated guidance on rabies post-exposure prophylaxis on Sept. 10. The rabies vaccine helps the body develop immunity to the virus, and the human rabies immune globulin provides immediate protection until the body's immune response takes effect. The CDC's guidance noted, however: "People who have been previously vaccinated or are receiving pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for rabies should not receive human rabies immune globulin (HRIG)." From July through August, the agency said it received 17 percent more rabies-related inquiries than during the same period last year. At least eight state health departments also reported increased use of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis, treatment errors, or both. The CDC said there is no national shortage of rabies vaccine or immune globulin, but says unnecessary treatment and mistakes can cause adverse effects, increase costs, and put pressure on supplies. “A typical course of PEP can cost between $11,000 and $14,000 per person,” the CDC stated. “Following rabies PEP administration guidance helps ensure that lifesaving vaccines are available for persons who need it and extraneous costs are avoided,” it added. Reported mistakes included injecting the vaccine in the buttocks, failing to place immune globulin around wounds, and administering both products at the same injection site. Other errors included omitting immune globulin when needed, giving it to previously vaccinated patients, and restarting vaccine series after a scheduling delay. Several outbreaks have been reported this year. In North Carolina, three baby goats from a mobile petting zoo tested positive for rabies Aug. 28, while a fourth was presumed infected, according to the state’s Department of Health and Human Services. The goats appeared at events in several counties from July 28 through Aug. 27, including an assisted-living facility and a back-to-school gathering. State officials said the animals were probably exposed after a skunk entered their pen. Because visitors may have bottle-fed, cuddled, or closely handled the goats, officials urged anyone with direct contact to seek an individual risk assessment. “Raccoons, skunks, and foxes continue to pose significant rabies threats to 75% of Americans,” the CDC states. Rabies can be transmitted from infected animals to humans and other animals through bites, scratches, or exposure to saliva. The virus primarily attacks the central nervous system, often resulting in brain inflammation and, if not treated promptly before symptoms appear, is almost always fatal. Each year, about 1.4 million people seek medical care after animal contact, and about 100,000 receive preventive rabies treatment, according to the CDC. The agency also reports roughly 4,000 rabid animals annually, more than 90 percent of them wildlife, such as in bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes

Several outbreaks have been reported this year. In North Carolina, three baby goats from a mobile petting zoo tested positive for rabies Aug. 28, while a fourth was presumed infected, according to the state’s Department of Health and Human Services. The goats appeared at events in several counties from July 28 through Aug. 27, including an assisted-living facility and a back-to-school gathering. State officials said the animals were probably exposed after a skunk entered their pen. Because visitors may have bottle-fed, cuddled, or closely handled the goats, officials urged anyone with direct contact to seek an individual risk assessment. “Raccoons, skunks, and foxes continue to pose significant rabies threats to 75% of Americans,” the CDC states. Rabies can be transmitted from infected animals to humans and other animals through bites, scratches, or exposure to saliva. The virus primarily attacks the central nervous system, often resulting in brain inflammation and, if not treated promptly before symptoms appear, is almost always fatal. Each year, about 1.4 million people seek medical care after animal contact, and about 100,000 receive preventive rabies treatment, according to the CDC. The agency also reports roughly 4,000 rabid animals annually, more than 90 percent of them wildlife, such as in bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes

news.content_zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 于 2026 年 9 月 10 日发布健康警报,称 2026 年夏季美国报告的人类 狂犬病 暴露量显着增加。这种激增促使 CDC 警告医疗保健提供者正确使用 狂犬病 和管理 狂犬病 暴露后预防 (PEP) 的重要性。CDC指出,与去年同期相比,狂犬病 疫苗和人狂犬病免疫球蛋白(HRIG)的使用量分别增加了33%和76%。至少有八个州卫生部门报告 PEP 使用增加、治疗 错误或两者兼有。CDC 强调,虽然全国范围内不存在这些 治疗 的短缺,但不必要的管理可能会导致不利影响、成本增加和供应紧张。该机构还强调,浣熊、臭鼬和狐狸仍然是 狂犬病 的主要威胁,75% 的美国人面临风险。疾病预防控制中心敦促接触过患有狂犬病的动物的个人寻求个人风险评估,特别是在北卡罗来纳州,那里的三只小山羊的 狂犬病 检测呈阳性,并且与涉及人类密切互动的事件有关。该警报强调需要准确的 PEP 协议,以确保有效保护并防止资源浪费。
